summary: Per-tool idempotency TTL causing duplicate function executions after streaming reconnects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated external side-effects (duplicate downstream POSTs to their order-processing webhook) after a streaming session resumes. Behavior occurs across Python, Go, and TypeScript SDKs.

Impact:
- Duplicate tool/function executions observed for a subset of streaming reconnects, causing duplicate orders for a small percentage (~0.6%) of resumed sessions.
- Affects production traffic in us-east for the NimbleRetail enterprise account. Customer is on an SLA and requests an urgent fix or mitigation.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod (us-east) serving gptx-13b-quant via streaming with function-calling.
- Customer uses the Python SDK (v1.4.2), Go SDK (v0.9.8), and TS SDK (v2.1.0) in parallel across microservices.
- Private HSM key rotation enabled for their account (rotation window: 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC).

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Start a streaming chat session and trigger a tool call that POSTs to /order/submit. SDK sends X-Idempotency-Token per function call.
2) Mid-stream, simulate a transient network drop (client loses socket).
3) Client reconnects after ~40 seconds using SDK resume logic.
4) Server replays buffered events and executes the tool again; downstream receives a second POST.

Observed logs (sanitized):
- server: resume_request id=session-7f3a, resume_window_ms=60000, matched_token=abc123, token_ttl_remaining_ms=1200
- serving-runtime: funccall-exec order_submit idempotency_key=abc123 status=executed
- customer webhook: POST /order/submit 200 idempotency=abc123 order_id=ord-1022
- after reconnect: serving-runtime: funccall-exec order_submit idempotency_key=abc123 status=executed
- customer webhook: POST /order/submit 200 idempotency=abc123 order_id=ord-1023

Notes on token generation and SDK behavior:
- SDKs generate per-tool idempotency tokens and attach them as X-Idempotency-Token metadata.
- Session resume uses a resumable offset and expects server-side stored idempotency entries to prevent duplicates.
- Customer's HSM rotation occurred close to the incident window which may have changed server-side token normalization for HSM-signed tokens.

Hypothesis:
1) Server TTL for per-tool idempotency entries can be shorter than the SDK resume window; when resume happens after TTL expiry, server treats the resumed call as new and re-executes.
2) HSM rotation introduced a change in the idempotency token signature or normalization, causing exact-match lookup to fail for some tokens generated before rotation.
3) Some edge proxies between client and Redwood may be rewriting or trimming the header, causing token mismatches on resume.

Immediate customer-facing workaround suggested:
- Have the customer set session-level idempotency (session-scoped key) rather than per-action short-lived tokens for long-lived streams, or increase resume timeout on the client to be < server TTL as a temporary measure.
- Enable server-side dedupe by explicit idempotency namespace (we can enable a per-customer extended TTL flag for enterprise accounts as a temporary mitigation).

Requested from engineering:
- Confirm server TTL for idempotency entries and whether HSM rotation can break lookups.
- Check edge proxy logs for header mangling in us-east for NimbleRetail.
- Evaluate quick patch to normalize HSM-signed token lookup across rotations.

investigation_notes:
- Verified default prod per-action TTL is 30s; many customers rely on resumed session <30s assumption.
- HSM rotation revealed an implementation detail: idempotency entries stored with 'token||key-id' which fails exact-match when key-id changed; changed lookup to compare on token prefix and optional key-id.
- Edge proxy (edge-proxy-4) had a rarely-hit code path that clipped headers >128 bytes; added a header-length log and mitigation ticket INT-43122.
- Repro validated across Python and Go SDKs; TS SDK had built-in session-scoped key helper but Python/Go lacked it prior to planned SDK updates.
workaround:
1) Short-term: We enabled enterprise extended-ttl flag for NimbleRetail (sets per-action idempotency TTL to 5 minutes) and applied key-id-tolerant lookup in us-east canary.
2) Customer guidance: adopt session-level idempotency tokens for long-lived streams or reduce reconnect delay below 30s until SDK patch is released.
resolution: In progress: canary normalizer deployed and enterprise TTL enabled for affected customer. Engineering will merge PR 812 to add session helpers in SDKs and harden server lookup across HSM rotations. Target full rollout: 2026-03-19. Postmortem and runbook to be published after rollout.
